questions.q: When the fuel supply was cut off, the generator faltered and finally ________ after only ten minutes.
questions.explanation: The past simple 'went out' matches the completed action described. 'Was going out' implies an ongoing action in the past; 'has gone out' is present perfect and not appropriate with the definite past time; 'goes out' is present simple and does not fit the past context.

questions.q: The committee disagreed with the proposal, ________ that it would be expensive and impractical.
questions.explanation: 'Arguing' correctly links the main clause to the reason clause; it is a present participle used to give the reason. 'And they argued' creates a separate clause and changes rhythm; 'argument' is a noun and ungrammatical here; 'to argue' would indicate purpose, not reason.

questions.q: When Mama Nkechi said the new road would be finished 'in a jiffy', she meant it would be finished _____.
questions.explanation: 'In a jiffy' is an idiom meaning 'very quickly'. The other options contradict the meaning: 'after a long time' and 'with great expense' are opposites, while 'only by chance' is unrelated.

questions.q: When he said he would 'bite the bullet' and accept the transfer to Sokoto, he meant he would _____.
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is an idiom meaning to face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage. The literal meaning about chewing is wrong; refusing or exaggerating do not convey the idiom's intent.

questions.passage: Mr. Adeyemi grew up in Ilesa and became a teacher at the town's only primary school. For many years he cycled thirty kilometres each day to reach the classroom and back. He believed education held the key to opportunity, so he often held evening classes for children who worked during the day. When the government announced a new scholarship for rural teachers, Mr. Adeyemi applied and won; the award paid his fees for a diploma course and improved textbooks for his pupils. Even after retirement he returned to help the school on special days, for he felt strongly that a community must look after its own institutions.
questions.q: Why did Mr. Adeyemi hold evening classes?
options: Because his daytime teaching job had been cancelled
Because the government required extra classes
Because some children worked during the day and could only attend lessons in the evening
Because he preferred teaching at night
questions.explanation: The passage states he held evening classes 'for children who worked during the day', so the correct answer matches that reason. There is no mention of job cancellation, government requirement, or a personal preference for night teaching.

questions.q: What benefit did the scholarship bring to the pupils?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says the award 'paid his fees for a diploma course and improved textbooks for his pupils.' It does not mention bicycles, a new building, or meals.

options: He preferred private tutoring to public service
He was dedicated to his community and to improving education
He wanted to leave Ilesa to seek fame elsewhere
questions.explanation: The passage shows dedication: long daily cycles, evening classes, winning a scholarship that benefited pupils, and returning after retirement. The wrong options contradict the passage's depiction.

questions.explanation: The passage states he 'cycled thirty kilometres each day'. The other distances are either too small or excessively large and do not match the text.

questions.q: Which word has the same primary stress pattern as 'Nigeria' (NI-ge-ria)?
questions.explanation: 'Nigeria' has stress on the first syllable (trochaic pattern). 'Camera' also has primary stress on the first syllable. 'Control' and 'occur' are stressed on the second syllable; 'create' is stressed on the second syllable as well.

questions.q: In the sentence 'I did tell the principal about the missing exams', which word carries emphatic stress to show the speaker really did inform the principal?
questions.explanation: Emphatic stress is often placed on auxiliary verbs like 'did' to confirm or insist that an action occurred. Stressing 'I' would emphasize the person; 'the' is unlikely to be emphasized; 'missing' would shift focus to the exams' status rather than the act of informing.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous' as used in: 'Mr. Olumide kept meticulous records of every pupil's attendance.'
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; 'scrupulous' matches that. 'Sloppy' and 'hasty' are opposites; 'indifferent' implies lack of care, which is also wrong.

questions.passage: Mrs. Amina ran a small evening school in Ibadan where pupils paid modest fees in naira. Many were children of traders who worked daytime markets; others were teenagers who had missed years of schooling. Each term she sent three deserving pupils to sit for a scholarship exam sponsored by a local firm. Winners received full support for the next year, which often included books and transport fare. Mrs. Amina believed the scholarship did more than ease expenses: it restored confidence and encouraged regular attendance. Even when the electric light failed, she improvised with kerosene lamps and continued teaching, convinced that interruptions should not rob children of learning.
questions.q: What is the main reason Mrs. Amina continued teaching despite the electric light failing?
options: She wanted to finish the syllabus quickly
She feared losing her scholarship sponsorships
She believed interruptions should not prevent children from learning
She needed the income from lessons that day
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states she was 'convinced that interruptions should not rob children of learning,' so her belief about learning is the main reason. The other options are not supported by the passage.

questions.q: According to the passage, which of the following was NOT listed as part of the scholarship support?
options: full support for the next year
questions.explanation: The passage lists 'books and transport fare' and 'full support for the next year'; it does not mention a housing allowance, so that is the correct answer.

questions.q: The word 'deserving' in the passage most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Deserving' refers to being worthy of help or recognition; it does not simply mean 'needy for money' or indicate behaviour or punctuality.

questions.explanation: The passage presents Mrs. Amina positively—highlighting her efforts and beliefs—so the author's attitude is admiring and approving. There is no critical or indifferent tone.

questions.q: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: 'By the time the parents arrived, the pupils _____ their presents to the teacher.'
questions.explanation: The action of giving occurred before another past event (parents arrived), so past perfect 'had given' is correct. 'Have given' is present perfect and doesn't fit; 'gave' is simple past but doesn't show the sequence; 'will have given' is future perfect and wrong here.

questions.q: Which word has the same final consonant sound as the underlined letter in 'book' (the 'k' sound)?
questions.explanation: 'Book' ends with the /k/ sound; 'back' also ends with /k/. 'Booklet' ends with /t/ sound; 'bought' ends with /t/ sound; 'boo' ends with a vowel sound.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'sparse' as used in: 'Vegetation along the road was sparse after the dry season.'
questions.explanation: 'Sparse' means thinly distributed; its antonym is 'abundant'. 'Thin', 'scattered', and 'meagre' are synonyms or near-synonyms of 'sparse', so they are incorrect here.

questions.q: Select the correct sentence:
options: Neither of the students have finished the assignment
None of the student have finished the assignment
Neither of the students are finishing the assignment
Neither of the students has finished the assignment
questions.explanation: 'Neither' with 'of the students' takes a singular verb: 'has'. 'Neither...have' is a common error. 'None of the student have' is wrong because 'student' should be plural and 'none' can take 'have' but the noun must agree. 'Neither...are finishing' uses the wrong verb form and number.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the underlined “ea” in “head”?
questions.explanation: The vowel in 'head' is the short /ɛ/ sound as in 'said'. 'Bead', 'read' (present) and 'heat' have the long /iː/ sound or diphthong /iː/, so they are incorrect.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the underlined 'o' in 'book'?
questions.explanation: 'Book' and 'could' share the short /ʊ/ vowel sound. 'Boot' has /uː/, 'boat' has /əʊ/ (or /oʊ/), and 'bore' has /ɔː/; these are different sounds.

questions.q: Which of the following has the same vowel sound as the underlined 'a' in 'father'?
questions.explanation: The 'a' in 'father' is the open back /ɑː/ vowel, which is the same in 'palm'. 'Cat' has /æ/, while 'mate' and 'name' have the diphthong /eɪ/.

questions.passage: Mr. Okonkwo is a retired banker who volunteers at the local community library in Ibadan. He collects old newspapers, catalogues donated books and helps young students prepare for exams. Each Saturday, he runs a free class where he emphasises accuracy and punctuality. Parents who visit say the atmosphere is calm and respectful. Several pupils who began as shy learners have improved and now help others. Mr. Okonkwo believes that small, steady steps lead to lasting progress, and he often reminds students that consistency matters more than sudden bursts of effort.
questions.q: Which word in the passage is formed from the verb 'donate'?
questions.explanation: The passage uses 'donated' (past participle/adjective) to describe books. While 'donating', 'donor', and 'donation' are all related forms, they do not appear in the passage; 'donated' is the exact form used.

questions.explanation: 'Express approval' fits the context that parents describe the atmosphere as calm and respectful. The other options contradict the positive description in the passage or are not natural collocations.

questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' is the correct spelling meaning very careful and precise. The other options are misspellings and are not correct British English forms.

questions.q: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: 'If Amina had known the bus would be late, she ________ earlier.'
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional structure (past unreal): 'If she had known... she would have left earlier.' 'Will leave' and 'would leave' are incorrect tense forms; 'had left' lacks the main clause auxiliary.

questions.q: Choose the correctly formed adjective from the noun 'courage'.
questions.explanation: The standard adjective form from 'courage' is 'courageous'. The other options are nonstandard or misspelled.

questions.q: Which sentence best explains the idiom 'bite the bullet' in a Nigerian context?
options: Accept an unpleasant duty because it is necessary
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure something painful or unpleasant that must be done. The other options are literal or unrelated interpretations.

questions.passage: Mrs. Aisha Musa taught at a small school on the outskirts of Ibadan. When she noticed that many pupils arrived hungry and tired, she began a modest breakfast club where parents could pay a small fee or donate ingredients. Over months the club became a community effort: a mechanic supplied firewood, a trader donated bread, and a retired nurse taught hygiene. Attendance improved, and pupils who had been quiet and listless grew lively in class. Though funds were limited, Mrs. Musa kept careful records and ensured fairness. Her initiative inspired a nearby school to start its own breakfast mornings. Local education officials praised the programme, saying it showed how simple acts could improve learning and strengthen neighbourhood ties.
questions.q: What was the main reason Mrs. Aisha Musa started the breakfast club?
options: Many pupils arrived at school hungry and tired.
Local officials ordered schools to feed pupils.
Parents wanted to meet every morning.
The school aimed to make money from fees.
questions.explanation: The passage states she noticed many pupils arrived hungry and tired and began the breakfast club for that reason. The other options are not supported: parents paying a small fee was allowed but not the main reason, and officials did not order it.

questions.passage: Mrs. Aisha Musa taught at a small school on the outskirts of Ibadan. When she noticed that many pupils arrived hungry and tired, she began a modest breakfast club where parents could pay a small fee or donate ingredients. questions.q: Which detail from the passage best shows that the breakfast club was fair and well managed?
options: Parents could pay a small fee or donate ingredients.
The mechanic supplied firewood every week.
Mrs. Musa kept careful records and ensured fairness.
questions.explanation: The sentence about careful records and ensuring fairness directly indicates good management. While other details show community support, they do not prove fairness and management practices.

questions.q: The phrase 'listless grew lively' in the passage most nearly means:
options: Pupils who were previously dull became active and interested.
Pupils stopped attending and then returned to school.
Learners became quieter and less participative.
Children began to sleep in class more often.
questions.explanation: 'Listless' means lacking energy; 'lively' means active and energetic. The phrase indicates a change from low energy to active engagement. The wrong options contradict that change or misinterpret it.

questions.q: Which of the following is an effect of the breakfast club mentioned in the passage?
options: A nearby school started its own breakfast mornings.
Mrs. Musa moved to Lagos to manage a larger programme.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states a nearby school was inspired to start similar breakfasts. The other options are not mentioned and contradict the passage's details.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'modest' as used: 'she began a modest breakfast club'.
questions.explanation: In context 'modest' means limited in size or scale; 'small-scale' is synonymous. 'Costly' and 'grand' are opposites, and 'famous' is unrelated.

questions.q: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to 'limited' in the sentence: 'Though funds were limited...'.
questions.explanation: 'Limited' here means not much; the antonym is 'abundant'. 'Meagre', 'restricted', and 'scarce' are synonyms or near-synonyms of 'limited', so they are incorrect.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Local education officials praised the programme, saying it showed how simple acts could improve learning and strengthen neighbourhood ties,' which idea is implied rather than directly stated?
options: The government funded the breakfast club completely.
Officials planned to replicate the programme nationwide immediately.
Community involvement can have wider benefits beyond the classroom.
The breakfast club failed to help pupils’ learning.
questions.explanation: The passage implies community involvement yields wider benefits; it does not state government funding, failure, or immediate nationwide plans. Those are not supported by the sentence.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'kept careful records' most likely suggest about Mrs. Musa's approach?
options: She relied entirely on others to run the club.
She hid the accounts from parents.
She preferred paperwork to meeting pupils.
She was organised and transparent in managing limited funds.
questions.explanation: 'Kept careful records' indicates organisation and transparency, especially given limited funds. The wrong options contradict the idea of careful record-keeping or make unsupported claims about neglect or secrecy.

questions.q: By the time the principal arrived, the students ________ their projects for the exhibition.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had finished' correctly shows that the action of completing projects happened before the principal's arrival. 'Finished' is simple past and doesn't establish the earlier-before-other-past action; 'have finished' is present perfect and wrong with a past time marker; 'were finishing' indicates an ongoing past action, not a completed one.

questions.q: If the school can raise 50,000 naira by Friday, it ________ the new textbooks next week.
questions.explanation: 'Will buy' is the correct future result in a real conditional (If + present, will + verb). 'Would buy' is for a hypothetical or unlikely situation; 'buys' is present simple and not appropriate for a future promise; 'is buying' (present continuous) could be used in some contexts but does not follow the standard first conditional pattern here.

questions.q: Neither the headmaster nor the teachers ________ willing to accept the sudden change in the timetable.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor' and the nearer noun 'teachers' (plural), the verb should be plural: 'were'. 'Was' would agree with a singular nearer noun; 'is' is present singular; 'have been' is present perfect and does not match the simple past context implied.

questions.q: Which word has the same final consonant sound as the final consonant in the word 'bag'?
questions.explanation: The final consonant sound in 'bag' is the voiced /g/ as in 'dog'. 'Back' and 'bat' end with voiceless /k/ and /t/ respectively; 'badge' ends with /dʒ/, a different sound. 'Dog' shares the voiced /g/ final sound.

questions.q: Which word has the same initial consonant sound as the underlined 's' in 'school' (pronounced /sk/)?
questions.explanation: The initial consonant cluster in 'school' is /sk/, the same as in 'skill'. 'Ship' and 'shoe' start with /ʃ/; 'city' starts with /s/ but followed by a /ɪ/ glide making the onset different; only 'skill' matches the /sk/ cluster.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'o' in 'book'?
questions.explanation: The vowel in 'book' is the short /ʊ/ as in 'could'. 'Boot' has /uː/ (long), 'broke' has /oʊ/, and 'back' has /æ/. Thus 'could' is the correct match.

questions.passage: Mrs. Aisha runs a small literacy programme in Kano that helps adults learn to read and write. Each month she records attendance, and she issues a paper certificate to those who complete a level. The certificates cost 200 naira each to produce, but many learners cannot afford this fee. To help, Aisha organises a small fundraiser where local bakers donate pastries and sellers give soft drinks; the proceeds pay for certificates for those who need them. The programme has grown slowly, yet steadily, and local officials now recognise its value.
questions.q: Choose the correctly formed adjective from the noun 'certificate'.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'certificated' (meaning having a certificate) is the standard formed adjective from 'certificate'. The other options are not standard English formations and are incorrect.

questions.passage: Mrs. Aisha runs a small literacy programme in Kano that helps adults learn to read and write. questions.q: Which of the following is the correct British spelling of the verb meaning 'to organise' as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage is written in British English and uses 'organise'. 'Organize' is the American variant but not the British spelling used here; 'organyse' and 'organnise' are misspellings.

questions.q: If the teachers had known about the strike earlier, they ______ the exam timetable to suit students.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional structure: 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle.' 'Had known' (past perfect) pairs with 'would have adjusted.' 'Would adjust' is a present conditional; 'had adjusted' is past perfect without modal; 'will have adjusted' is future perfect and doesn't match the conditional.

questions.q: The governor promised to repair the bridge ______ funds were released from the state treasury.
questions.explanation: 'Once' means as soon as/after funds are released and correctly connects the time clause. 'Unless' introduces a condition meaning 'if not' (wrong meaning). 'Though' and 'however' express contrast, not the timely sequence required.

questions.q: The new shopkeeper sold her goods quickly because she ______ the best prices in the market.
questions.explanation: 'Offered' fits logically: selling quickly because she offered the best prices. 'Resisted' and 'ignored' are opposite actions, and 'borrowed' is unrelated to pricing; none of these explain why goods sold fast.

questions.q: When Musa said he would 'burn the midnight oil' to finish his assignment, he meant he would
questions.explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' is an idiom meaning to work or study late at night. The wrong options take the phrase literally or give unrelated meanings (study at dawn or discard notes).

questions.q: When the coach told the team to 'keep their cards close to their chest' before the final match, he wanted them to
questions.explanation: The idiom 'keep one's cards close to one's chest' means to be secretive or not reveal plans. The wrong options misunderstand the idiom literally or suggest the opposite (play openly or discuss publicly).

questions.passage: Mrs. Amaka runs a small tailoring workshop in Benin City where she trains unemployed youths. Each trainee pays a token fee, and in return receives materials and practical lessons. She keeps careful registers of attendance and progress to ensure that the best learners qualify for a micro-credit scheme that helps them start a business. Last year, three of her former apprentices opened their own tailoring shops nearby and now employ others. Mrs. Amaka believes that steady, honest work rebuilds dignity and supports families more reliably than uncertain handouts.
questions.q: According to the passage, why does Mrs. Amaka keep registers of attendance and progress?
options: to write articles about their lives
to report trainees to the government
to identify the best learners for the micro-credit scheme
to charge extra fees from absent trainees
questions.explanation: The passage states she keeps registers to ensure the best learners qualify for a micro-credit scheme. The other options are not mentioned; charging extra, reporting to government, or writing articles are unsupported and unlikely given the context.

questions.passage: Mrs. Amaka runs a small tailoring workshop in Benin City where she trains unemployed youths. Each trainee pays a token fee, and in return receives materials and practical lessons. options: Three former apprentices opened their own tailoring shops and now employ others
Mrs. Amaka keeps registers of attendance
She trains unemployed youths in Benin City
Trainees pay a token fee for lessons
questions.explanation: The detail about former apprentices opening shops and employing others directly shows positive community impact. The other statements describe the workshop's methods or target group but do not demonstrate positive outcomes.

options: helps people feel respected and independent

questions.q: Which word has the same primary stress pattern as 'Lagos' (LA-gos)?
questions.explanation: 'Lagos' has primary stress on the first syllable (LA-gos). 'Kano' likewise has stress on the first syllable. 'Abuja' and 'Onitsha' have stress on the second syllable, while 'Port Harcourt' places stress on the second syllable of 'Harcourt.'

questions.q: If the Parent-Teacher Association can raise 75,000 naira by Monday, the school ______ buy the new science equipment before the term starts.
questions.explanation: The conditional structure requires future result: 'If ... can raise ..., the school will be able to ...' 'Is able to' is present and doesn't fit the future consequence; 'will able to' is ungrammatical (missing 'be'); 'can being able to' is ungrammatical and redundant.

questions.q: When the new principal told a joke during assembly, it helped to 'break the ice' between her and the students. What does 'break the ice' most nearly mean here?
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' is an idiom meaning to ease tension and make people feel relaxed. It does not mean ending relationships, beginning formal proceedings, or announcing bad news.

questions.passage: At Eze Primary School in Owerri, a small workshop teaches basic tailoring and carpentry to young people after school. The project began when a retired teacher, Mrs. Okoro, donated an old sewing machine and some tools. Local artisans volunteer as instructors twice a week, and trainees pay a token fee to cover thread and nails. The programme aims to give practical skills, boost confidence and reduce idle time among youth. Parents praise the project because some trainees have begun repairing furniture or sewing school uniforms for neighbours. School officials keep simple records of attendance and progress so successful trainees can be put in touch with employers or saved funds for buying more materials.
questions.q: According to the passage, why do the trainees pay a token fee?
options: to buy new machines for the workshop
to register formally with the local government
to cover the cost of materials such as thread and nails
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states trainees pay 'a token fee to cover thread and nails.' It does not say the fee pays instructors' salaries, buys new machines, or is for formal government registration.

questions.q: By the time the state governor inspects the school on Monday, the contractors ________ repairs to the collapsed culvert on the access road.
questions.explanation: The sentence requires the future perfect to show that the repairs will be finished before a specified future time ('by the time... on Monday'), so 'will have completed' is correct. 'Will complete' could be used but does not emphasise completion before the governor's arrival; 'will be completing' indicates an ongoing action at that time; 'would have completed' is conditional and inappropriate here.

questions.q: Which word has the same primary stress pattern as 'nigeria' (ni-GE-ria)?
questions.explanation: 'nigeria' has primary stress on the second syllable (ni-GE-ria). 'complete' also has primary stress on the second syllable (com-PLETE). 'monitor' and 'harmony' have primary stress on the first syllable, and 'teacher' has primary stress on the first syllable as well.
